runtime.execution: In-process candidate engine with adapters, selection/evaluation callbacks and saved state; alternate optimize-anything engine can supervise Claude Code subprocesses.
runtime.service_boundary: Owns candidate selection/budget/checkpoint, consumes user evaluator and model/agent implementation.

summary: Named-component candidate evolution, reflective feedback and independent test scoring are useful autodroit mechanisms; selection authority and evaluator trust must stay explicit.

inspection.scope: Read adapter/evaluation protocol, acceptance criteria, actual batch selection/dedup/rejection path, main checkpoint loop, state save, held-out scoring and autoresearch subprocess watchdog.
inspection.limits: Not all adapters/engine variants inspected; no model/evaluator invocation, benchmark reproduction or complete filesystem isolation audit.

actions.name: GEPAAdapter.evaluate / make_reflective_dataset / propose_new_texts
actions.output: Scores/outputs/optional trajectories and proposed text components

actions.name: GEPAEngine.run / selection_strategy.select
actions.input: Seed/validation data, strategy programs and stop callbacks
actions.lifecycle: Checkpointed iterations; custom selection may permit exploration.

actions.name: optimize_anything
actions.input: Seed, evaluator, objective, engine/budgets and held-out test set
actions.output: Best candidate/score, pool/metadata and independent test scores

filesystem.detail: Framework writes candidate/checkpoint records and external-agent engine materializes workspace; not a universal model file-tool interface.

processes.detail: Alternate autoresearch engine supervises actual Claude subprocess with session ID, budget and watchdog; inherited agent tool execution not claimed as GEPA implementation.

code_actions.detail: Candidate text can be executable code through user adapter/evaluator; generic engine does not itself provide a persistent kernel.

persistent_kernel.detail: persistent_kernel: this reference supplies reflective program optimization framework; an agent policy, model interface and context lifecycle are outside its supplied role.

standing_database.detail: Structured candidate state and eval ledger exist, but no independent standing query service for agent work was established in inspected engine/state/budget paths.

workflow_programming.detail: Adapters, proposer, acceptance and selection strategies are programmable runtime interfaces; custom selection may override acceptance.

multi_model.detail: Proposer/evaluator models are separately supplied/configured; not an independent live collaboration bus.

live_collaboration.detail: live_collaboration: this reference supplies reflective program optimization framework; an agent policy, model interface and context lifecycle are outside its supplied role.

concurrent_work.detail: Batch proposal/evaluation interfaces support grouped work and an independent external process; concurrency scheduling is adapter/engine-specific.

steering_interrupt.detail: Subprocess watchdog can terminate wedged/budget-exhausted external agent; no general operator steering to busy candidate/model work in inspected paths.

turn_redefinition.detail: Caller can replace selection/proposal/evaluation programs; this is optimizer policy, not model hot-redefinition of its live conversation turn.

compaction.detail: compaction: this reference supplies reflective program optimization framework; an agent policy, model interface and context lifecycle are outside its supplied role.

context_repair.detail: context_repair: this reference supplies reflective program optimization framework; an agent policy, model interface and context lifecycle are outside its supplied role.

original_audit.detail: Optional trajectories and candidate/log callbacks depend on adapter capture; score-only evaluations and caller-defined traces cannot guarantee all original IO.

audit_query.detail: Candidate state, iteration records and callbacks are program accessible; not all original provider/OS IO.

hot_change.detail: Strategies/adapters/candidates are caller-programmable, but adopted candidate is a future evaluation artifact, not after-turn hot replacement of current harness.

rebuild_continuity.detail: Pickled candidate state excludes runtime hooks and external agent uses transcript session resume; no executable refit/context/ongoing-work transfer.

remote_services.detail: remote_services: this reference supplies reflective program optimization framework; an agent policy, model interface and context lifecycle are outside its supplied role.

self_improvement.detail: Executable reflect/propose/evaluate/select loop can optimize prompts/programs/harness components through supplied adapters; no automatic safe activation in current harness.

complaints.detail: complaints: this reference supplies reflective program optimization framework; an agent policy, model interface and context lifecycle are outside its supplied role.

authority.detail: Strategy owns selection, evaluator owns score semantics, engine owns budget/watchdog and supplied subprocess permission posture.

evaluation.detail: Independent evaluator supplies scores, subsample selection then validation/test split; exceptions score zero, objective validity remains caller responsibility.

time_order.detail: Eval ledger has wall timestamps; external-agent watchdog uses monotonic elapsed time, without durable paused-time policy.

evidence.claim: Adapter supplies candidate execution, scores, optional trajectories and proposer component edits; evaluator outputs are opaque to engine.
Built-in acceptance compares summed subsample scores, with strict or lateral-move criterion.
Selection strategy is authority and may surface criterion-rejected proposals; selected input identities/dedup and truthful rejection callbacks enforced.
Engine saves adapter/candidate state before iteration and stops according to callback policy.
Checkpoint pickles state excluding runtime hooks, optionally clouds callable data; image/live process continuity not promised.
Eval call ledger is thread-safe; proposer dollars have separate owner/cap, not same budget.
Claude subprocess pins session/resume, remaining USD cap and watchdog on monotonic no-eval time; permissions depend on sandbox mode.
Held-out tests evaluated directly outside engine budget/server; exceptions map to zero scores.
Known score vectors exercise strict/equal/worse/marginal acceptance.

tests.oracle: Known vectors distinguish strict improvement, equality, regression and 0.0001 gain; tests do not validate the external evaluator or generalization.
Mock selectors/samplers verify same-parent shape and differing minibatches; not actual parallel provider/task execution.

strengths: Selection, acceptance, evaluator, reflection and budgets have distinct programmable owners.
Unselected proposals receive explicit reasons; optional held-out scoring stays outside optimization input.
limits: Custom selection can override acceptance; a strict criterion is not an inviolable gate by itself.
Optimizing score may exploit an invalid evaluator; saved candidate records are not original all-IO audit.
arconaut_questions: Which experiment governance decisions belong to the model, and which independent machine invariants cannot be overridden?
How does self-improvement keep selected/rejected/failed candidates observable without conflating metrics with correctness?
